first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and simplifying onboarding has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. I will verify that evidence alongside promotional-pricing evidence because pricing is highly consequential under the new competitor pressure but may trade durable qualified revenue for lower-quality or less-retained acquisition. The experiment should measure qualified activation and downstream revenue, not completion alone.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing this cycle: although it raised qualified revenue initially, verified evidence shows a 12% 30-day retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. It is the only verified option that directly improves the concurrent onboarding and activation declines while also increasing 30-day retention, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The deeper competitor cut raises the urgency of SMB churn, but the verified promotional-pricing result produced a 12% retention decline and failed at first renewal; escalating discounting would risk sacrificing durable value for a short-term response. Track price-sensitive SMB churn as a guardrail and reassess pricing next cycle when verification capacity returns.
